relations.why: A .query() call with an interpolated template literal is reported by both rules.
relations.settle: Keep both: a parameterized query ($1 placeholders with a values array) satisfies both, and PG-CONCAT-001 also catches + concatenation.

source.paraphrase: Pass values as a params array against $1 placeholders. Concatenating values into the SQL string sends them as code, which is injection.

invariants.why: A concatenated or interpolated value is parsed as SQL, so a quote in user input escapes the literal and runs attacker SQL.
invariants.fixHint: Rewrite the statement with $1, $2 placeholders and pass the values as the second query argument. Keep identifiers static or allowlist them.
invariants.avoid: Backticks with ${} are still concatenation; only a params array parameterizes. The rule reads the first .query argument (or the text field of a config object), through parentheses, casts, ternaries and ??/||/&& fallbacks; values in the params array are not read. SQL built in a variable or inside a helper call is not seen, and any tagged template passes as a parameterizing tag.

source.paraphrase: Keep TLS verification on for database links. Disabling it sends credentials and rows over a connection anyone on the path can read or rewrite.

invariants.why: sslmode=disable, ssl false, or rejectUnauthorized false leaves the database link cleartext or MITM-able, exposing credentials and row data.
invariants.fixHint: Use sslmode=require or verify-full in the URL, or ssl with rejectUnauthorized true and the CA. Scope any exception to local-only config, not code.
invariants.avoid: Moving the disable into the connection URL is the same open link as the ssl flag.

source.paraphrase: Bound how long a statement and an idle client may live. Without a timeout one runaway query holds its connection forever and starves the pool.

invariants.why: A pool with no statement or idle timeout lets one stuck query pin a connection indefinitely until the pool is exhausted.
invariants.fixHint: Set statement_timeout for statements and idleTimeoutMillis for idle clients on every Pool, sized from the slowest legitimate query.
invariants.avoid: Tuning max alone sizes the pool; it does not bound a runaway statement.

source.paraphrase: PostgreSQL does not support parameters for identifiers. Dynamic database, schema, table or column names need pg-format escaping instead of $n placeholders.

invariants.why: A $n placeholder always carries a value. FROM $1 or INSERT INTO $1 fails with a syntax error, and ORDER BY $1 sorts by a constant, so the rows come back unsorted without any error.
invariants.fixHint: Keep table and column names static, choose them from a fixed allowlist, or escape them with pg-format's %I. Keep $n placeholders for values only.
invariants.avoid: ORDER BY $1 runs without an error but does not sort by the named column. Placeholders after FROM inside EXTRACT, substring or trim, followed by a cast, or in FROM unnest($1) are values and pass. The rule reads literal query text in the .query arguments; text built in a variable is not seen.
